newsitem.title: FRANCE: Southern France forest fires drop in rainy summer.
newsitem.headline: Southern France forest fires drop in rainy summer.

text.p: A rainy summer has dramatically cut forest fires, the scourge of southern France, this year, firemen said on Wednesday.
They said fire had ravaged 3,000 hectares (7,500 acres) so far this year in the 15 southeastern departments controlled by their firefighting coordination centre.
Some 10,000 hectares (25,000 acres) had gone up in smoke last year and 20,000 hectares (50,000 acres) in 1994.
With the summer over, large forest fires were now unlikely. The firemen said the drop in fires was due to poor weather, lack of wind and an improvement in prevention measures.
